title: Imaginarity witnessing enhancement via spectral norms of witnesses
authors: Yuhang Xie, Yanjun Chu, Yushan Ding, Shao-Ming Fei
abstract: Quantum imaginarity is an essential physical resource that underpins key functionalities of modern quantum technologies. We improve imaginarity witnessing via the prior knowledge of imaginarity-witness operators. To this end, we derive a rigorous upper bound on the maximum expectation value of an imaginarity witness operator over the set of all free (real) quantum states, which is given by the spectral norm of the real component of the corresponding witness operator. We demonstrate via detailed examples that this bound substantially improves imaginarity detection. We further classify all imaginarity-witness operators into four distinct families based on this bound. For these four witness classes, we perform a comprehensive analysis of their completeness and finite completeness, the joint detection of shared imaginary quantum states by different witnesses, and the conditions for distinct witnesses to identify identical imaginary states. Our results advance the fundamental understanding of imaginarity detection and offer useful insights for both theoretical studies and experimental implementations of quantum imaginarity.
summary: This paper advances the theory of quantum imaginarity detection by introducing a rigorous enhancement based on the spectral norm of the witness operator. It derives a new detection criterion, $	ext{Tr}[Who] > \| 	ext{Re}(W) \|_\infty$, which significantly improves the ability to identify imaginary quantum states. The authors classify all relevant witness operators based on this spectral norm bound.
main_problem: The paper aims to improve the detection of quantum imaginarity—a resource quantified by the imaginary component of quantum states—using prior knowledge of spectral norms of witness operators.
main_result: The knowledge of the spectral norm, $\| 	ext{Re}(W) \|_\infty$, provides a rigorous and enhanced detection criterion for imaginary states, leading to a classification of all imaginarity-witness operators into four distinct families.
method: The authors derive a new detection criterion by establishing an upper bound on the expectation value of an imaginarity witness over all real states, which is given by the spectral norm of the real part of the witness operator.
model_or_system: The study concerns quantum states ($ho$) in a $d$-dimensional Hilbert space, distinguishing between real states ($\mathcal{R}$) and imaginary states ($\mathcal{D} \setminus \mathcal{R}$). Detection relies on Hermitian 'imaginarity witnesses' ($W$).
key_observables: The expectation value $	ext{Tr}[Who]$, the spectral norm $\| 	ext{Re}(W) \|_\infty$, and the trace $	ext{Tr}[W]$ are key observables.
important_parameters: The spectral norm $S = \| 	ext{Re}(W) \|_\infty$ acts as a crucial parameter defining the enhanced detection regime.
main_assumptions: The method assumes the existence of a suitable upper bound $S$ derived from the spectral norm of $	ext{Re}(W)$ to enhance the standard detection criterion $	ext{Tr}[Who] < 0$.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the comparison between the traditional detection criterion ($	ext{Tr}[Who] < 0$) and the enhanced criterion ($	ext{Tr}[Who] > S$), and map out the relationship between various bounds ($\mu_{\max}$, $\| 	ext{Re}(W) \|_\infty$, $	ext{Tr}[W]$) for different state types.
paper_structure: The paper introduces the problem, derives the spectral norm bound, establishes the enhanced detection criterion, classifies the witnesses into four families, and proves theorems regarding the completeness and finite completeness of the resulting detection scheme.
why_interesting: This work provides a fundamental theoretical tool for quantifying and detecting non-classical resources like imaginarity, which has direct implications for understanding the operational boundaries of quantum information processing beyond standard coherence measures.
